back: Money borrowed from outside the business that must be repaid, normally with interest (loans, overdrafts, debentures, mortgages, hire purchase).
Money raised by selling a share in ownership (share capital, new partners, venture capital); no fixed repayment but profit and control are shared.
Short-term borrowing up to an agreed limit; flexible, interest on the amount used, can be withdrawn at short notice.
Paying for an asset by a deposit and instalments; the business owns it at the end; total cost exceeds the cash price.
Paying regular rent to use an asset owned by someone else; no large outlay but no ownership at the end.
Investment by specialists in risky new businesses in return for shares and the chance of a high return.
A company's long-term loan certificate paying fixed interest and repayable on a set date.
Short: overdraft, trade credit, factoring. Medium/long: bank loan, hire purchase, leasing, mortgage, debentures, share capital.
Amount needed, time period, cost, risk, security available, form of business and willingness to give up control.
